description: Continuously consumes messages from Kafka topics, decoding Avro, JSON, or Protobuf payloads (optionally via a Confluent Schema Registry) into one document per message.

transports.purpose: The record source: the Kafka cluster itself, reached with librdkafka via a BaseConsumer.

spec.endpointConfig: A single free-form comma-separated `bootstrap_servers` host:port list (no default port supplied by the connector). The wire security protocol is derived, not configured: (credentials, tls) -> SASL_SSL / SASL_PLAINTEXT / SSL / PLAINTEXT. The client is always created with enable.auto.commit=false, group.id="source-kafka" (a placeholder librdkafka demands), and statistics.interval.ms=300000 for lag logging.

transports.purpose: Confluent Schema Registry: consulted at discovery time (GET /subjects, then GET /subjects/{topic}-key|-value/versions/latest) to learn each topic's key/value schema, and inline during the capture (GET /schemas/ids/{id}, cached per id) to decode the Confluent wire framing of each message. Optional — when `schema_registry_type` is `no_schema_registry` this transport is absent and all payloads are parsed as JSON.

baseUrl.resolution: the user-supplied `schema_registry.endpoint` config field, e.g. https://registry-id.us-east-2.aws.confluent.cloud; the connector concatenates paths onto it verbatim

continuity.ourSideLoss: Unread messages are silently lost. The broker's own retention.ms / retention.bytes deletes segments regardless of our read position, and an assignment for an offset the broker has since discarded resumes at whatever is still retained — a gap in the captured stream that reports as a clean sync.
continuity.resumeWindow: The retention window of each captured topic (retention.ms / retention.bytes), which is set by the customer and is not read, validated, or surfaced by the connector.
continuity.notes: There is genuinely no lease. The consumer is built with enable.auto.commit=false and never commits an offset; `group.id` is set to the literal "source-kafka" only because librdkafka rejects an empty value. Partitions are attached with a manual `assign()` of an explicit TopicPartitionList rather than `subscribe()`, so the connector never joins a consumer group, never writes to __consumer_offsets, and holds no broker-side group or rebalance state. The code comments say so directly: librdkafka's own `consumer_lag` statistic is deliberately ignored because it is derived from a committed offset this connector never writes. Read position lives entirely in Flow's connector checkpoint (`bindingStateV1` -> {stateKey: {partitions: {partitionId: offset}}}), emitted as a merge-patch after every single message and resumed as Offset(offset+1), or Offset::Beginning for a partition with no stored offset. Consequence: stopping costs the customer nothing — nothing accrues on their brokers, no segments are held open, no group is left rebalancing — so `releasedOnShutdown` is vacuous (there is nothing to release). The entire risk is on our side and is a deadline, not a backlog: pause longer than the topic's retention and the unread data is gone. This is the mirror image of the WAL/binlog abandonment risk.

configFields.name: bootstrap_servers
configFields.description: Comma-separated initial Kafka cluster servers to connect to; the client learns the rest of the cluster from one of these.

configFields.name: credentials.auth_type
configFields.description: Discriminator selecting the credential variant: "user_password" (SASL user & password) or "AWS" (AWS MSK IAM). `credentials` is listed as required in the published JSON schema, but the Rust type is Option: when omitted entirely the client falls back to PLAINTEXT/SSL, documented as dev/test only.

configFields.name: credentials.mechanism
configFields.description: SASL mechanism for the user_password variant: PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, or SCRAM-SHA-512. Defaults to PLAIN. Required within that variant.

configFields.name: credentials.aws_access_key_id
configFields.description: AWS access key id used to mint an MSK IAM OAUTHBEARER token locally (AWS variant).

configFields.name: credentials.aws_secret_access_key
configFields.description: AWS secret access key used to mint an MSK IAM OAUTHBEARER token locally (AWS variant).

configFields.name: credentials.region
configFields.description: AWS region of the MSK cluster (AWS variant). The AWS variant additionally requires tls=system_certificates: the connector aborts unless the derived protocol is SASL_SSL.

configFields.name: tls
configFields.description: Only accepted value is "system_certificates" (also the schema default). Combined with credentials it selects the security protocol: SASL_SSL (creds+tls), SASL_PLAINTEXT (creds only), SSL (tls only), PLAINTEXT (neither).

configFields.name: schema_registry.endpoint
configFields.description: Confluent Schema Registry API endpoint, e.g. https://registry-id.us-east-2.aws.confluent.cloud. Base URL of the sidecar transport.

configFields.name: schema_registry.username
configFields.description: Schema registry HTTP basic-auth username; the 'Key' of a Confluent Cloud schema registry API key.

configFields.name: schema_registry.password
configFields.description: Schema registry HTTP basic-auth password; the 'Secret' of a Confluent Cloud schema registry API key.

configFields.name: schema_registry.enable_json_only
configFields.displayName: Capture Messages in JSON Format Only
configFields.description: Must be literally true when no schema registry is configured; a false value is rejected during deserialization with a custom error. Acknowledges that all payloads will be parsed as JSON and that discovered collections are keyed by message partition & offset.

configFields.name: topic
configFields.description: Per-binding resource config (not endpoint config): the Kafka topic to capture messages from. resource_path_pointers is ["/topic"].

discovery.method: Kafka Metadata API via the consumer client (fetch_metadata over all topics, 60s timeout), then — only when a Confluent Schema Registry is configured — HTTP GET /subjects on the registry, plus GET /subjects/{topic}-key|-value/versions/latest and GET /schemas/ids/{id} (10 concurrent) for each topic that has a matching subject.
discovery.querySketch: list cluster topics -> drop internal topics -> sort -> intersect registry subject names against the topic list by stripping the '-key'/'-value' suffix -> fetch the latest key and/or value schema for each matching topic (an unsupported schema is logged and skipped rather than failing discovery) -> emit one binding per topic with resource config {topic}, resource path [topic], recommended name = topic, and a document schema carrying x-infer-schema plus a required /_meta envelope (topic, partition, offset, op) and a conditional reduce {delete:true, strategy:'merge'} when _meta.op == 'd' -> collection key = the non-object leaf JSON pointers of the registered message-key schema when that schema passes a usability check, else the default ['/_meta/partition','/_meta/offset'].

authTierRationale: Every supported credential is a value the user can self-serve from their own cluster: a SASL username/password (PLAIN or SCRAM-SHA-256/512), or an AWS access key id/secret/region for MSK IAM. The one OAuth-shaped path (sasl.mechanism=OAUTHBEARER) is not user-registered OAuth — the connector mints an MSK SigV4 bearer token itself from the supplied AWS keys via a ClientContext callback, and the spec response reports oauth2: None. The optional schema registry adds only a basic-auth key/secret pair. No app registration and no refresh token anywhere.

unionMisfits.description: v2's `pull.partitioned_log` finally describes what this connector does, but it is only reachable as a member of `streams[].pull`, and per rule 7 a fully-discovered stream transport has an empty `streams` list — the connector names no topic literally. So the one pull shape that applies uniformly to every binding has nowhere to be recorded. The same gap swallows the fact that a tombstone (absent payload) sets _meta.op='d' and the discovered schema turns that into a reducing delete, since `partitioned_log` has no `emitsDeletes` field the way `changes` does. Proposed: a connector-level `defaultPull` used when streamMode is 'discovered' and every binding shares one shape. Its verified value for this connector is given below.

incremental.unit: one Kafka topic-partition; a binding is one topic, assigned as an explicit TopicPartitionList via manual assign() (never subscribe())
incremental.offsetKind: int64 Kafka offset per partition, stored in the Flow connector checkpoint as bindingStateV1 -> {stateKey: {partitions: {partitionId: offset}}}; resumed as Offset(offset+1), or Offset::Beginning when the partition has no stored offset
incremental.notes: Partitions of one binding may be split across concurrent connector shards: HighwayHash over (topic name bytes || little-endian partition id) with a hard-coded 32-byte key, top 32 bits of the hash taken, and the partition skipped unless the hash falls in [range.key_begin, range.key_end]. With no RangeSpec the shard takes every partition. A checkpoint merge-patch is written after every single message. A null message payload is a tombstone: it sets _meta.op='d' and the discovered document schema reduces it as a delete.

unionMisfits.description: v2's split of `json_pointers` vs `synthetic` correctly names both halves of this connector's bimodality — a usable registered message-key schema yields the leaf JSON pointers of that key (json_pointers), and everything else falls back to the synthetic broker coordinates ['/_meta/partition','/_meta/offset'] — but which branch a topic takes is decided at discovery time from the customer's registry contents, and `writeDisposition` still has to be one constant. json_pointers means the collection has real record identity and reduces/merges by it, honouring tombstones as deletes; synthetic means every message is unique and the stream is effectively append-only. There is no way to say 'merge or append, decided per stream at discovery'.

Still unrepresentable in v2. Payload decoding is polymorphic and decided per message at runtime from the Confluent wire framing (magic byte 0 followed by a 4-byte big-endian schema id), yielding Avro, JSON, or Protobuf from the same topic; protobuf schemas additionally resolve their registry references depth-first into a FileDescriptorSet. Message-key fields are merged over the payload at the document root and clobber colliding payload fields; a non-record Avro/JSON key is wrapped as {_key: value}; broker metadata (topic, partition, offset, op, headers as UTF-8-or-base64, CreateTime/LogAppendTime timestamp) is injected under /_meta. None of this record-shaping has a home in transports, credentialModes, or any pull member.

description.snippet: This is a flow connector that reads from Kafka topics/partitions.

transports[1].spec.baseUrl.snippet:
let fetched: FetchedSchema = self
    .make_request(format!("{}/schemas/ids/{}", self.endpoint, id).as_str())

execution.schedule.snippet:
.poll(None)
.expect("polling without a timeout should always produce a message")

execution.continuity.customerSideAccrual.snippet:
config.set("enable.auto.commit", "false");
config.set("group.id", "source-kafka"); // librdkafka will throw an error if this is left blank

discovery.querySketch.snippet:
let subject = format!("{}{}", topic, if key { TOPIC_KEY_SUFFIX } else { TOPIC_VALUE_SUFFIX });
let version = self.fetch_latest_version(subject.as_str()).await?;

abstained.streams: Streams are entirely customer-defined: one binding per non-internal topic present in the customer's cluster at discovery time. The connector names no production stream. The seven topics in tests/test.flow.yaml (avro-topic, json-schema-topic, json-raw-topic, protobuf-topic, protobuf-ref-topic, protobuf-wkt-topic, avro-ref-topic) are integration-test fixtures created by the docker-compose harness, not shipped streams, so listing them would misrepresent them. The uniform per-binding pull shape is recorded in unionMisfits[0] instead, since v2 offers no container for it.
abstained.streams[].primaryKey / primaryKeyKind: Not knowable statically — it is bimodal. `json_pointers` (the non-object leaf pointers of the topic's registered message-key schema) when the registry has a key schema that passes the usability check (no nullable types, every location either required or defaulted, keyable scalar types, additionalProperties:false); `synthetic` (['/_meta/partition','/_meta/offset']) otherwise, including whenever no schema registry is configured or the key schema fails to fetch/parse. Which branch applies depends on the customer's registry contents at discovery time.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: No single cursor field exists. The resume position is a map partitionId -> Kafka offset held in the Flow checkpoint; /_meta/offset and /_meta/partition are surfaced in the document but neither alone is a usable cursor. Recorded as partitioned_log.offsetKind in unionMisfits[0] instead.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: Depends on the same branch as primaryKeyKind: merge (with tombstone deletes) when a registered message key gives the collection real identity, effectively append when the synthetic partition/offset key makes every document unique. Not determinable without the customer's registry.
abstained.streams[].supportedSyncModes: Neither 'full_refresh' nor 'incremental' describes the behaviour. There is no refresh; an unseeded binding starts at Offset::Beginning, which is the earliest offset the broker still retains — not full history and not a snapshot — then continues indefinitely.
abstained.execution.continuity.releasedOnShutdown: Vacuous rather than unknown: the connector leaves no server-side artifact to release (no consumer group membership, no committed offsets, no open segment holds). Recorded as null rather than true to avoid implying a release step exists.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: The window is real but its length is set entirely by the customer's per-topic retention.ms / retention.bytes. The connector never reads, validates, or warns on retention, so no bound can be stated from the source.
abstained.transports[0].spec defaultPort: Not expressible and not supplied: bootstrap_servers is a free-form comma-separated host:port list with no connector-side default. Port 9092 appears only in the local docker-compose test harness.
abstained.transports[1].spec.apiVersionPinning: The registry client pins no API version — no Accept header (e.g. application/vnd.schemaregistry.v1+json), no version path segment. The only query parameter used is ?format=serialized on protobuf schema fetches, which selects an encoding, not a version.
abstained.discovery.querySketch (registry-absent p: With no schema registry configured, discovery degrades to the Kafka metadata listing alone: every non-internal topic is discovered with the synthetic partition/offset key and JSON-only parsing. The sketch given covers the registry-enabled path.
